To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of people in the community with anxiety do not seek treatment, even though they are disabled, and those who do consult are more likely to receive effective treatment if they consult a mental health specialist rather than another health professional.
Anxiety disorders are common, disabling and highly treatable, yet only a minority of individuals with these conditions seek treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epidemiology and service utilisation of anxiety disorders.
the identification and measurement of anxiety and the treatment of anxiety disorders.
the identification of the determinants of help seeking for anxiety disorders in Australia, and the relationship between help seeking and effective treatment for anxiety disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more severely disabled individuals seek treatment for their anxiety symptoms.
there is a need to increase the rates of treatment seeking for anxiety, particularly among the disabled, comorbid, and those with more severe disorders.
there is a need for a comprehensive and detailed study to determine whether the results are conclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
anxiety disorders are common, disabling and under-recognised and treated.
anxiety is a common disorder that has a significant impact on the lives of individuals.
the majority of people with anxiety disorders do not receive appropriate treatment, even though treatment is effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more severely symptomic and comorbid persons with anxiety disorders do consult for treatment.
the most important factor in treatment seeking is severity of symptoms, and that the most important barrier to care is the belief that symptoms can be managed without professional help.
there are still a large number of people who are suffering with anxiety disorders and are not receiving treatment.
